name: Typography
description: A compact, modern typography system for product interfaces, data-heavy views, navigation, forms, and readable long-form content.
rationale: Use Mona Sans as the primary interface typeface because it combines excellent readability at small sizes with a modern product-oriented character and enough personality to establish a recognizable visual identity without becoming decorative. Keep the scale intentionally restrained so hierarchy comes from size, weight, spacing, and contrast rather than oversized headings. Use a system monospace stack for code and technical content without requiring an additional font dependency.
guidance:
Use Mona Sans throughout product UI, navigation, forms, tables, dashboards, and readable prose. Use the monospace family for code, logs, technical identifiers, keyboard input, and content where fixed character widths improve comprehension. Use 14px for compact interface text and controls, 16px for standard body content, and 12px only for supporting metadata, captions, and low-emphasis labels. Use 20px for section headings, 24px for prominent headings and dialogs, and 32px for major page titles; avoid oversized typography in normal application UI. Use regular 400 for body text, entered values, text inputs, textareas, placeholders, helper text, and other editable content. Use medium 500 for field labels, buttons, controls, and navigation. Use semibold 600 for headings and reserve bold 700 for exceptional emphasis. Use sentence case. Use approximately 1.5 line height for body text, 1.4 for compact interface text, and 1.2 to 1.3 for headings. Keep long-form prose near 60 to 70 characters per line. Use tabular numerals for metrics, tables, dashboards, and changing numeric values. Establish hierarchy with the smallest effective change in size, weight, spacing, or color rather than increasing font size unnecessarily.

Use Mona Sans for all interface labels, navigation, section labels, overlines, controls, and user-facing content. Reserve monospace typography for code, logs, technical identifiers, keyboard input, and content where fixed character widths provide functional value. Do not use monospace merely to create visual hierarchy or a technical aesthetic.
notes: Primary typeface is Mona Sans. Recommended web stack: "Mona Sans", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif. Mona Sans provides the intended cross-platform visual identity while the fallback stack uses high-quality native or commonly available fonts when it cannot load. On Apple platforms, the system fallback naturally uses the platform system typeface. The scale is optimized for modern information-dense product interfaces rather than editorial or marketing layouts.
